chunks: Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Ayyūb ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: “I have greater authority over every believer than his own self. Whoever leaves behind wealth, it belongs to the heir, and whoever leaves behind debt or dependents in need, then it comes to me and is upon me.”

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: having greater authority and claim over each believer than the believer has over himself
key_terms.الْوَارِثِ: the legal heir who inherits the estate
key_terms.دَيْنًا: an unpaid debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.ضَيَاعًا: dependents or vulnerable persons left without support
key_terms.مَالًا: property or wealth left behind by the deceased

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say about a believer’s debts, heirs, and his authority over them?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the authority and responsibility of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم over the believers. It states that a deceased person’s wealth goes to the legal heirs, while unpaid debt and vulnerable dependents fall under the Prophet’s care and responsibility.
